elements.quote: Our goal was to systematically review contemporary literature comparing the relative effectiveness of two mechanical compression devices (LUCAS and AutoPulse) to manual compression...
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly frames the report as a systematic review (and the title states 'A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis').

elements.quote: Our goal was to systematically review contemporary literature comparing the relative effectiveness of two mechanical compression devices (LUCAS and AutoPulse) to manual compression for achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective/review question explicitly.

elements.quote: We only included studies in the English language that reported ROSC outcomes in adult patients in non-trauma settings
elements.reason: Key inclusion criteria (English, ROSC outcome, adults, non-trauma, RCTs and observational studies, OHCA) are specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: We searched medical databases systematically for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and observational studies published between January 1, 2000-October 1, 2020
elements.reason: The abstract mentions searching medical databases and a date range but does not name the information sources (e.g., PubMed, Embase) or state when each source was last searched.

elements.quote: We assessed for risk of biases in randomization, allocation sequence concealment, blinding, incomplete outcome data, and selective outcome reporting.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the domains used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: to conduct random-effects metanalysis and trial sequence analysis (TSA). Multivariate meta-regression was performed using preselected covariates to account for heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the synthesis methods (random-effects meta-analysis, TSA, meta-regression).

elements.quote: A total of 15 studies (n = 18474), including six RCTs, two cluster RCTs, five retrospective case-control, and two phased prospective cohort studies, were pooled for analysis.
elements.reason: The abstract reports total studies, participants, and study design characteristics.

elements.quote: The pooled estimates' summary effect did not indicate a significant difference (Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio = 1.16, 95% confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.39, P = 0.11, I2 = 0.83) between mechanical and manual compressions during CPR for ROSC.
elements.reason: Results for the main outcome (ROSC) are reported with number of studies/participants pooled.

elements.quote: Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio = 1.16, 95% confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.39, P = 0.11
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: Mechanical compression devices for resuscitation in cardiac arrests are not associated with improved rates of ROSC.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect (no benefit favoring either group; mechanical devices not superior).
The abstract does not summarize limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Mechanical compression devices for resuscitation in cardiac arrests are not associated with improved rates of ROSC. Their use may be more beneficial in non-ideal situations such as lack of bystander CPR, unwitnessed arrest, and delayed EMS response times.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not state the primary source of funding for the review.

elements.quote: We chose ROSC for 20 minutes or more after resuscitation in an OHCA as the primary outcome.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis was performed for studies reporting ROSC of patients in both groups assuming independence of results from other reported endpoints.
elements.reason: The manuscript never states whether all results compatible with the ROSC outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought from each study; it only describes which studies entered the meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Meta-analysis was performed for studies reporting ROSC of patients in both groups assuming independence of results from other reported endpoints.

elements.quote: The following data points were extracted: name of the first author; year of study; sample size; number of participants per treatment arm; study design; type of device used; time delay in mechanical compressions; inclusion and exclusion criteria; average age, gender (percentage female); percentage of witnessed arrests; the percentage receiving bystander CPR; percentage with an initial shockable rhythm; time in minutes of EMS arrival; and primary outcome (ROSC).

elements.quote: In all cases, meta-analyses were performed using the MantelHaenszel (M-H) method for dichotomous data to estimate pooled odds ratios (OR).

elements.quote: Authors (MS, JC) participated in each phase of the review (screening, eligibility, and inclusion).
